\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{উত্তেজনা} (uttejônā)}{উত্তেজনা (uttejônā)}]{\bn{উত্তেজনা} (uttejônā) — excitement; tension}

\label{lesson:BN-C298-uttejona}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a public statement, then the Bengali for to mention.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{উত্তেজনা}}
\textbf{\bn{উত্তেজনা}} — \emph{uttejônā} — \textquotedblleft{}excitement; tension\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{খবরটা} \bn{শুনে} \bn{পাড়ায়} \bn{উত্তেজনা} \bn{ছড়াল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{khôbôrṭā shune pāṛāy uttejônā chhôṛālô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When the news came, tension spread through the neighbourhood.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{উত্তেজনা}} (\emph{uttejônā}) is Sanskrit \emph{uttejana} (feminine \emph{uttejanā}), 'incitement, stimulation' (Monier-Williams), from \emph{ut-} 'up' and \emph{tejas} 'sharpness, heat': a stirring up.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uttejônā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uttejônā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khôbôrṭā shune pāṛāy uttejônā chhôṛālô.} — When the news came, tension spread through the neighbourhood.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a public statement, then the Bengali for to mention, then say \emph{uttejônā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{রটানো} (rôṭāno)}{রটানো (rôṭāno)}]{\bn{রটানো} (rôṭāno) — to spread a rumour; to put about}

\label{lesson:BN-C298-rotano}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to mention, then the Bengali for tension.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{রটানো}}
\textbf{\bn{রটানো}} — \emph{rôṭāno} — \textquotedblleft{}to spread a rumour; to put about\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{কেউ} \bn{রটাল} \bn{যে} \bn{চোর} \bn{আবার} \bn{আসবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{keu rôṭālô je chor ābār āsbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Someone put it about that the thief would come back.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{লোক} \bn{খবরটা} \bn{রটাল}, \emph{sei lok khôbôrṭā rôṭālô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{রটানো}} (\emph{rôṭāno}) is usually linked with Sanskrit \emph{raṭati}, 'cries, yells' (CDIAL 10590): what is shouted about gets about.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rôṭāno}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to mention, then the Bengali for tension, then say \emph{rôṭāno} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{হইচই} (hôichôi)}{হইচই (hôichôi)}]{\bn{হইচই} (hôichôi) — an uproar; a commotion}

\label{lesson:BN-C298-hoichoi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for tension, then the Bengali for to spread a rumour.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{হইচই}}
\textbf{\bn{হইচই}} — \emph{hôichôi} — \textquotedblleft{}an uproar; a commotion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{খবরটা} \bn{শুনে} \bn{পাড়ায়} \bn{হইচই} \bn{পড়ে} \bn{গেল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{khôbôrṭā shune pāṛāy hôichôi pôṛe gelô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When the news came, the neighbourhood was in an uproar.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{হইচই}} (\emph{hôichôi}) is an expressive word, like English \emph{hubbub}: its sound is the noise. \bn{হইচই} \bn{পড়ে} \bn{যাওয়া}, an uproar breaks out. No dictionary we use records an older form, so its history is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hôichôi}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for tension, then the Bengali for to spread a rumour, then say \emph{hôichôi} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ফিসফিস} \bn{করা} (phisphis kôrā)}{ফিসফিস করা (phisphis kôrā)}]{\bn{ফিসফিস} \bn{করা} (phisphis kôrā) — to whisper}

\label{lesson:BN-C298-phisphis-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to spread a rumour, then the Bengali for an uproar.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ফিসফিস} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{ফিসফিস} \bn{করা}} — \emph{phisphis kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to whisper\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ক্লাসে} \bn{ছাত্ররা} \bn{ফিসফিস} \bn{করে} \bn{গল্প} \bn{করছিল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{klāse chhātrôrā phisphis kôre gôlpo kôrchhilô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In class the students were whispering to each other.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{মেয়ে} \bn{ফিসফিস} \bn{করল}, \emph{sei meye phisphis kôrlô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ফিসফিস} \bn{করা}} (\emph{phisphis kôrā}) puts \bn{ফিসফিস}, an imitative word for the hiss of a whisper, before \bn{করা}. \bn{ফিসফিস} \bn{করে} \bn{বলা}, to say something in a whisper. No dictionary we use records an older form, so its history is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling what happened.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{চাঞ্চল্য} (chānchôlyô)}{চাঞ্চল্য (chānchôlyô)}]{\bn{চাঞ্চল্য} (chānchôlyô) — a sensation; a stir}

\label{lesson:BN-C298-chancholyo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for an uproar, then the Bengali for to whisper.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{চাঞ্চল্য}}
\textbf{\bn{চাঞ্চল্য}} — \emph{chānchôlyô} — \textquotedblleft{}a sensation; a stir\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দুর্ঘটনার} \bn{খবরে} \bn{শহরে} \bn{চাঞ্চল্য} \bn{ছড়াল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{durghôṭônār khôbôre shôhôre chānchôlyô chhôṛālô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
News of the accident caused a stir in the town.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{চাঞ্চল্য}} (\emph{chānchôlyô}) is Sanskrit \emph{cāñcalya}, 'unsteadiness, restlessness' (Monier-Williams); a town in a stir is a restless town.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chānchôlyô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{durghôṭônār khôbôre shôhôre chānchôlyô chhôṛālô.} — News of the accident caused a stir in the town.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for an uproar, then the Bengali for to whisper, then say \emph{chānchôlyô} again
\end{itemize}
